sonuc: Violation of Article 5 - Right to liberty and security (Article 5-1 - Lawful arrest or detention)
paragraflar: (Application no. 46378/18)
This judgment is final but it may be subject to editorial revision.
In the case of Akgül v. Türkiye,
The European Court of Human Rights (Second Section), sitting as a Committee composed of:
Jovan Ilievski, President, Péter Paczolay, Juha Lavapuro, judges, and Dorothee von Arnim, Deputy Section Registrar,

the application (no. 46378/18) against the Republic of Türkiye lodged with the Court under Article 34 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (“the Convention”) on 21 September 2018 by a Turkish national, Mr Aydın Akgül (“the applicant”), who was born in 1978 and is detained in Samsun, and was represented by Mr M. Yıldız, a lawyer practising in Istanbul;

the decision to give notice of the complaints under Article 5 of the Convention concerning the lawfulness of the pre-trial detention, the alleged lack of reasonable suspicion regarding the commission of an offence, the alleged lack of information in respect of the reasons for the applicant’s arrest, the alleged lack of relevant and sufficient reasons when ordering and extending the pre-trial detention, the ineffectiveness of the judicial review of the lawfulness of the detention, and the lack of an effective remedy for compensation to the Turkish Government (“the Government”), represented by their Agent at the time, Mr Hacı Ali Açıkgül, former Head of the Department of Human Rights of the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Türkiye, and to declare the remainder of the application inadmissible;
the parties’ observations;
the decision to reject the Government’s objection to the examination of the application by a Committee;
Having deliberated in private on 20 October 2026,
Delivers the following judgment, which was adopted on that date:
SUBJECT MATTER OF THE CASE

1. The present application mainly concerns the arrest and pre-trial detention of the applicant in the aftermath of the coup attempt of 15 July 2016, on suspicion of his membership of an organisation described by the Turkish authorities as the “Fetullahist Terror Organisation / Parallel State Structure” (Fetullahçı Terör Örgütü / Paralel Devlet Yapılanması, hereinafter referred to as “FETÖ/PDY”), which was considered by the authorities to be behind the coup attempt (further information regarding the events that unfolded after the coup attempt, including the details of the state of emergency declared by the respondent State and the ensuing notice of derogation given to the Secretary General of the Council of Europe, as well as the legislative developments that followed the declaration of the state of emergency, may be found in Baş v. Turkey (no. 66448/17, §§ 6‑14 and 109‑10, 3 March 2020). The applicant was serving as a judge at the material time.

2. On 16 July 2016 the Ankara chief public prosecutor’s office initiated a criminal investigation into, inter alia, the suspected members of FETÖ/PDY within the judiciary, in accordance with the provisions of the ordinary law, on the grounds that there had been a case of discovery in flagrante delicto falling within the jurisdiction of the assize courts (further information regarding the orders issued by the chief public prosecutor’s office within the context of that investigation, as well as the ensuing suspensions and dismissals of judges and prosecutors suspected of being members of FETÖ/PDY, may be found in Baş, cited above, §§ 9-10 and 15-21). In the context of the investigation opened by the Ankara public prosecutor’s office, the Edirne public prosecutor initiated a criminal investigation in respect of the applicant on suspicion of being a member of FETÖ/PDY, an offence punishable under Article 314 of the Criminal Code (see for the text of that provision ibid., § 58).

3. On 20 July 2016 the Edirne Magistrate’s Court decided to place the applicant in pre-trial detention on suspicion of membership of a terrorist organisation. The judge relied mainly on the fact that the applicant had been suspended from his duties as a judge on the grounds of his membership of the organisation that had instigated the attempted coup and that the Ankara chief public prosecutor’s office had requested the launching of a criminal investigation in that regard. Regard being had to the state of the evidence, the nature of the offence with which he had been charged – which was among the so-called “catalogue” offences listed in Article 100 of the Code of Criminal Procedure –, the potential sentence and the ongoing investigations across the country into the coup attempt, the judge held that pre-trial detention was a proportionate measure.

4. The applicant lodged an individual application with the Constitutional Court in respect of, inter alia, an alleged violation of his right to liberty and security on various accounts, including the alleged unlawfulness of his detention by reason of the disregard of the procedural safeguards afforded to members of the judiciary in domestic law. The individual application was declared inadmissible (compare also Turan and Others v. Turkey, nos. 75805/16 and 426 others, §§ 26-27, 23 November 2021).
ALLEGED VIOLATION OF ARTICLE 5 § 1 OF THE CONVENTION

5. The applicant complained under Article 5 § 1 of the Convention that he had been placed in pre-trial detention in breach of the domestic law governing the arrest and pre-trial detention of members of the judiciary and disputed that there had been a case of discovery in flagrante delicto for the purposes of section 94 of Law no. 2802 on judges and prosecutors (see for the text of this provision Baş v. Turkey, no. 66448/17, §§ 66-67, 3 March 2020).

6. The Government, firstly, invited the Court to declare this complaint inadmissible on the ground that the applicant had not made use of the compensatory remedy provided for under Article 141 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the alternative, they argued that the application should be declared inadmissible as an abuse of the right of application, submitting that the applicant had failed to inform the Court of developments in his case following the lodging of the application. As to the merits, the Government maintained that there had been no violation of Article 5 § 1 of the Convention since the applicant had been arrested and placed in pre-trial detention in compliance with the applicable law. Lastly, the Government requested that the applicant’s complaints under Article 5 be examined in the light of the derogation notified by Türkiye under Article 15 of the Convention.

7. As to the Government’s pleas of inadmissibility, the Court notes that similar objections raised by the Government were previously dismissed in Turan and Others (cited above, §§ 57-64) and sees no reason to depart from those findings in the present case. The Court accordingly considers that this complaint is not manifestly ill-founded within the meaning of Article 35 § 3 (a) of the Convention or inadmissible on any other grounds. It must therefore be declared admissible.

8. As to the merits, the Court reiterates that, in Baş (cited above, §§ 143‑58) and Turan and Others (cited above, §§ 79-92), it found that the notion of in flagrante delicto under section 94 of Law no. 2802 had been interpreted extensively by the domestic courts in a manner incompatible with Article 5 § 1 of the Convention. After examining the parties’ submissions in the present case, the Court sees no reason to depart from that conclusion. It notes in particular that the applicant, who benefited from the procedural safeguards afforded to members of the judiciary by Law no. 2802, was nevertheless placed in pre-trial detention under the ordinary rules of criminal procedure on the basis that he had allegedly been caught in flagrante delicto. However, the domestic courts did not establish that the applicant had been apprehended while committing, or immediately after committing, an act directly linked to the coup attempt. The Court further observes that the finding of in flagrante delicto was decisive in depriving the applicant of the safeguards provided by Law no. 2802. In these circumstances, and having regard to its findings in Baş and Turan and Others, the Court concludes that the applicant’s pre-trial detention did not take place in accordance with a procedure prescribed by law within the meaning of Article 5 § 1 of the Convention.

9. Regarding the Government’s request that the Court examine the present complaint in the light of the derogation by Türkiye under Article 15 of the Convention, the Court reiterates that, while the applicant was detained a short time after the coup attempt – that is, the event that prompted the declaration of the state of emergency and the notice of derogation by Türkiye, which is undoubtedly a contextual factor that should be fully taken into account in interpreting and applying Article 5 of the Convention in the present case – the measure at issue cannot be said to have been strictly required by the exigencies of the situation (see Baş, cited above, §§ 115-16 and 159-62, and Turan and Others, cited above, § 91).
10. Having regard to the foregoing, there has been a violation of Article 5 § 1 of the Convention on account of the unlawfulness of the applicant’s initial pre‑trial detention.

11. As regards any remaining complaints under Article 5 §§ 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 of the Convention, the Court decides not to examine them, in view of its findings under Article 5 § 1 above and its considerations in Turan and Others (cited above, § 98).
APPLICATION OF ARTICLE 41 OF THE CONVENTION
12. The applicant did not submit a claim for just satisfaction within the time-limit allotted. Accordingly, the Court considers that there is no call to award him any sum on that account.
FOR THESE REASONS, THE COURT, UNANIMOUSLY,
Declares the complaint under Article 5 § 1 of the Convention concerning the lawfulness of the applicant’s initial pre-trial detention admissible;
Holds that there has been a violation of Article 5 § 1 of the Convention on account of the unlawfulness of the applicant’s initial pre-trial detention;
Holds that there is no need to examine the admissibility and merits of the applicant’s remaining complaints under Article 5 of the Convention.
Done in English, and notified in writing on 17 November 2026, pursuant to Rule 77 §§ 2 and 3 of the Rules of Court.
Dorothee von Arnim Jovan Ilievski Deputy Registrar President
